title_tag: Site work and utility installation | 9 Arrow Land Service
meta_description: Site work and utility installation in Central Texas. Pads, grading, stock tanks, septic and propane excavation, and trenching for waterlines and conduit.
h1: Site work and light utility installation for Central Texas land
lede: Site work and utility installation from 9 Arrow covers the dirt work between cleared land and a finished project. We cut pads, shape terrain and trench for waterlines, conduit and septic lines, and your licensed plumber or electrician makes the final connections.

answer.q: What site work and utility installation does 9 Arrow do?
answer.a: 9 Arrow site work and utility installation covers grading, pad sites, stock tanks, creek crossings and excavation up to about 4 feet deep. We trench for low-pressure waterlines 3 inches or smaller, electrical conduit and septic lines. We do not install electrical wire, make final water or electrical tie-ins, or excavate swimming pools.

highlights: Excavation up to about 4 feet deep
Pads, stock tanks and creek crossings
Works with your licensed plumber and electrician

paras: 9 Arrow site work runs on dozers and excavation equipment that work in rocky terrain and difficult soil, both common across the Hill Country. We reshape terrain, handle selective site grading and shaping, and cut pads, including garage pads. We install and fine-grade pad sites for foundations and future buildings.

Pad work usually follows clearing. If the building site still has trees and brush on it, start with [land clearing for a building site](site-prep), and see our post on [land clearing cost in Texas](blog-land-clearing-cost-texas) for what drives that price. Rocky ground is normal around our home base, and local conditions are covered on our [land clearing in Spring Branch](land-clearing-spring-branch-tx) page.

sections.h2: Stock tanks, water features and creek crossings
paras: Rural site work often means holding water or getting across it. 9 Arrow grades stock tanks, small lakes and water features with dozers and excavation equipment. We also build creek crossings that establish access where none existed before.
A crossing is only useful if a road reaches it. Clearing, grading, culverts and road base for the route itself are covered on our [access road building](roads-and-access-preparation) page.

sections.h2: Trenching and excavation for light utilities
paras: Light utility installation at 9 Arrow means trenching and excavation. We trench for low-pressure waterlines 3 inches or smaller, for electrical conduit and for septic lines. We excavate for propane tanks and septic systems. Our excavation runs up to about 4 feet deep.

The trench is the 9 Arrow part of a utility job. Licensed plumbers and electricians handle the connections, and we coordinate with them, along with engineers, general contractors and site supervisors, so our trenching, pads and grading fit their plans.

sections.h2: What our site work and utility installation does not include
paras: 9 Arrow is plain about the limits of our site work and utility installation. Three jobs fall outside it and belong to licensed trades and specialists. Knowing that up front lets you line up the right people before the trench is open. 9 Arrow does not take on the three jobs below.
bullets: Installing electrical wire, which belongs to a licensed electrician
Final water or electrical tie-ins, which belong to licensed plumbers and electricians

sections.h2: Who uses site work and light utility installation
paras: Site work and light utility installation from 9 Arrow serves private landowners preparing a home site or outbuilding, ranchers grading stock tanks and creek crossings, and land developers and commercial real estate teams who need pads, trenching and grading done ahead of their trades.

On larger projects, 9 Arrow works alongside engineers, general contractors and site supervisors. On smaller ones, we work directly with the landowner and their licensed plumber or electrician. Either way, we price after a discovery call or site visit. Call (210) 247-8410 to talk through your site.

faqs.q: Do you make the final water and electrical connections?
faqs.a: 9 Arrow does not make final water or electrical tie-ins, and we do not install electrical wire. Our part is the trenching for low-pressure waterlines 3 inches or smaller, electrical conduit and septic lines. We coordinate with your licensed plumber and electrician, who make the final connections once the trench work is done.

9 Arrow excavates up to about 4 feet deep with dozers and excavation equipment that work in rocky terrain and difficult soil. Typical work includes trenching for waterlines, electrical conduit and septic lines, and excavating for propane tanks and septic systems. Projects that need deeper digging should be planned with your engineer or general contractor.

9 Arrow does not excavate swimming pools. Our site work covers pads, selective grading and shaping, stock tanks, small lakes and water features, creek crossings, and excavation for propane tanks and septic systems. For a pool, work with a pool contractor, and we can still handle clearing and grading on the rest of the site.

faqs.q: Can you build a pad for a house or garage?
faqs.a: Yes, 9 Arrow cuts pads, including garage pads, and installs and fine-grades pad sites for foundations and future buildings. If the pad site still has trees and brush, the site needs clearing first. Pad work pairs well with a driveway or access road, since a building site also needs a way in.

faqs.q: What size waterline can you trench for?
faqs.a: 9 Arrow trenches for low-pressure waterlines 3 inches or smaller. The trench is dug with excavation equipment that works in rocky terrain and difficult soil, and our excavation runs up to about 4 feet deep. Your licensed plumber makes the final water tie-in, since 9 Arrow does not make final water connections.
